name: Kaş
title: Holidays in Kaş
intro: Turquoise coves, ancient ruins in town and boat trips over a sunken city. Here's what Kaş is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: Check the latest travel advice and entry rules for Turkey on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: June, September and October are hot without being too much, and the sea is warm. July and August are very hot, so plan a long lunch in the shade. Winter is mild but wet, and many places close.

things.name: Kekova boat trip
things.blurb: Glide over the sunken ruins of an ancient city and stop for swims in clear bays.

things.name: Kaputaş Beach
things.blurb: A small sandy cove with bright blue water between the cliffs. There are lots of steps down from the road.

things.name: Antiphellos Theatre
things.blurb: An ancient Greek theatre in town, facing the sea. Good for sunset.

things.name: Patara Beach
things.blurb: A huge sandy beach with dunes, Roman ruins and nesting sea turtles.

things.name: Saklıkent Gorge
things.blurb: Wade up a narrow canyon in icy river water. Bring water shoes.

things.name: Snorkelling and diving
things.blurb: Clear, calm water full of fish. Dive centres run taster sessions for older children.

faqs.question: Is Kaş good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, for families who like swimming, boats and a relaxed small town. Most of the coast is rocky, so it suits confident swimmers better than toddlers who want sand.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: A week gives time for boat trips, a couple of beach days and Patara or Saklıkent. Stay ten nights to slow down.

faqs.question: How do you get there from the UK?
faqs.answer: Fly to Dalaman or Antalya, about four hours from the UK, then drive or transfer for two to three hours. British passport holders don't need a visa for short stays.

faqs.question: Where can children swim?
faqs.answer: Hotels and beach clubs have swimming platforms and ladders into deep water. For sand, head to Kaputaş or Patara. Water shoes help on the rocks.
